title: Checking isomorphisms on constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be admissible, let
$F_1,F_2:\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$ be exact functors
preserving direct sums, and let $\eta:F_1\to F_2$ be a natural transformation
of exact functors. If $\eta_K$ is an isomorphism for every
$K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, then it is an isomorphism for every
$K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: Put S = Dctf(X,Lambda) and P = Loc(S). Apply [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] to obtain that P is replete, triangulated and closed under all existing ambient coproducts. The full inclusion is fully faithful and exact by [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Its inherited triangulations are those in the statement.

Apply the proved small-support argument of [lem-exc-coproduct-preservation-universe-extension] to each restricted-domain functor. In any existing coproduct the nonzero summands inject into its endomorphisms by coordinate idempotents. Thus their index type is small in the Hom universe u+1. Remove zero summands, shrink this support, use the assumed coproduct preservation and restore zero summands. This gives preservation of every existing coproduct indexed in the ambient object universe u+2, without asserting existence of all such coproducts. The recorded Lean helpers are private, so their complete proofs are reproduced as private helpers in this module.

source.place: Private helpers coproduct_small_support and preservesCoproducts_of_small; also the private helpers in lean/Sheaf/Paper/UnboundedLocalizingPullback.lean.

proof.text: The upstream NatTrans.isoLocus instances make the isomorphism locus replete and triangulated: shift compatibility gives shift stability, zero is carried to zero, and [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] gives triangle closure. Map this property along the fully faithful exact inclusion P.ι into the ambient derived category; Mathlib ObjectProperty.map preserves triangulated structure and is replete. For a diagram of objects in this image with an existing ambient coproduct, lift the diagram to P using repleteness. The inclusion creates its coproduct by ambient closure of P. Lift the witnessing isomorphisms to see each component of the diagram lies in isoLocus. Mathlib isIso_app_coconePt_of_preservesColimit, using Step 2, gives invertibility at its colimit. The preserved colimit comparison puts the ambient coproduct in the image. Consequently the image of isoLocus is a localizing ambient property.

Each ambient generator K has its canonical lift to P, by the containment clause of [det-def-localizing-closure-existence]; hη makes its component invertible, so S is contained in the ambient image of isoLocus. The defining intersection [sk-def-localizing-closure] puts every source object in this ambient image. Lift its witnessing isomorphism through P.ι and apply repleteness of isoLocus. This proves every component invertible, without extending either functor to the ambient derived category.
